name: Codeine
label: Sub Pop
lede: Codeine played so slowly that Sub Pop, the grunge label, asked them to fly to Seattle and add fuzz. They declined, and made three records before they quit in 1994.

eras.title: A $98 bass and an idea about slowness
eras.text: Codeine grew out of Oberlin friendships and a New York couch. Stephen Immerwahr wanted music that barely moved, and found two people patient enough to play it.

years.h: Stephen Immerwahr arrives at Oberlin with a $98 Vox bass
years.p: That Vox Beatle bass would carry Codeine. At Oberlin, Immerwahr overlapped with [[Chris Brokaw|a05544f2-9341-4c9d-8ba0-7621a23012c6]], [[Sooyoung Park|403de443-6062-4f06-bd45-be02974a9441]] of [[Bitch Magnet|6be97715-b3fe-421b-b478-c4462ee9de15]], [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and [[Liz Phair|149326c2-b8a3-48e3-b3d2-9b5b9593127f]].

years.h: Immerwahr meets John Engle, who is crashing on a New York couch
years.p: Engle's brother was an Oberlin alum, which is how he ended up in the city. Immerwahr says he knew on meeting [[John Engle|b6261573-22eb-4d89-9f67-feb11b3ac92d]] that he wanted a band with him.

years.h: Squid becomes Codeine, and Chris Brokaw takes the drum stool
years.p: Immerwahr and Engle had played as Squid with drummer Peter Pollack. Oberlin grad Brokaw, son of a bebop drummer, joins on drums.
years.xp:
Immerwahr had been an assistant engineer since 1988, on sessions for bands like [[Soul Asylum|b10db9ad-b4c3-47f3-a7a4-37864b134f65]] and Living Colour. The slowness was deliberate. "I was interested in the slowness of emotional depressive states. The slowness of opiate drug states," he told Numero Group.

He also wanted the intensity that comes from playing slow on purpose.

years.h: Codeine opens for Bitch Magnet at the Middle East
years.p: The first show, in Cambridge, is under Bitch Magnet and Green Magnet School. [[Doug Scharin|979a7fb2-872d-454d-8c01-96cfed8a53d9]], the future drummer, is in the crowd.

eras.title: A basement, then the hottest label in town
eras.text: Codeine made its first record in a basement for almost nothing, and a German label put it out. Then Sub Pop signed the band, and wanted it to sound more like the rest of the roster.

years.h: Recording Frigid Stars in a basement with a dirt floor
years.p: [[Mike McMackin|6b450a4a-56ed-4745-8d3e-fcc9f0247ee9]] set the band up in his apartment building's basement: an eight-track, a dehumidifier between takes, overdubs in the boiler room. There was no budget to speak of.
years.xp:
McMackin's own description of the room: a dirt floor and a "very dark, cramped, dungeon-ous atmosphere."

The sessions ran over two stretches, June and August 1990.

years.h: Frigid Stars LP comes out in Germany first
years.p: Glitterhouse issues it after the Pickup Song 7-inch. The title comes from a line by [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]], and Melody Maker called the record "a rare and astonishing achievement."
years.xp:
Immerwahr researched star imagery at the New York Public Library for the sleeve. The back cover is Engle's photo of a friend on a mattress in an Avenue A apartment.

NME was less sure what to do with the vocals, calling Immerwahr a "scrawny sounding vocalist" who "oozes murmured poetry."

years.cap: Codeine in a Sub Pop press photo
years.h: Sub Pop signs Codeine, then asks for more fuzz
years.p: Jonathan Poneman and Bruce Pavitt saw Codeine's fifth show at TT the Bear's in Cambridge and signed them. Poneman then asked if the band would fly to Seattle and add guitar with [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]]. They said no.
years.xp:
"It was totally weird. I think we and Beat Happening were sort of the first non-grunge bands to get signed to that label," Immerwahr told the Village Voice.

Sub Pop's US edition in May 1991 added 3 Angels and a distorted-guitar version of Pea, but the album itself stayed as the band made it. Immerwahr later noted the deal gave Sub Pop the records in perpetuity. The upside was that they never went out of print.

years.h: Codeine opens for the Jesus Lizard to a puzzled Boston crowd
years.p: Fans there are puzzled by the Sub Pop deal. The band also plays under [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]] and [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]], and tours Europe that fall with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]]' band [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]].

years.h: Brokaw's other band, Come, puts out Car on Sub Pop
years.p: Chris Brokaw has moved to guitar alongside [[Thalia Zedek|a22a05de-b2e2-437c-91fc-df7b67ceb584]] in Come. John Engle could already tell he wouldn't stay in Codeine.

eras.title: The year every session went wrong
eras.text: Codeine spent 1992 in New York and Boston studios and hated most of what came out. An album got shelved, the drummer left, and a 25-minute EP kept the band going.

years.big: "I thought it was the best thing we'd done."
years.h: Codeine records a second album, then scraps it
years.p: That's Chris Brokaw on the sessions at Harold Dessau Recording in Manhattan, with Mike McMackin. Stephen Immerwahr scrapped them anyway.
years.xp:
"It was heartbreaking, for me anyway, when we shelved it," Brokaw told Brooklyn Vegan. Immerwahr didn't want the album to be the band's last word.

Immerwahr later said all of Codeine's 1992 recordings went badly. The songs, including Sea, Tom and Wird, were re-recorded with a new drummer.

years.h: Doug Scharin of Rex takes over the drums
years.p: Josh Madell of Antietam fills in on a US tour after Chris Brokaw leaves for Come. Then Scharin, who'd seen Codeine's first Boston show, takes over.

years.h: Barely Real: 25 minutes from a bad year
years.p: Pieced together from sessions at Toxic Shock and Harold Dessau in New York and a Boston studio. [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] arranges the piano piece W.
years.xp: Melody Maker called it "25 minutes of snowblind glory."

eras.title: One more record, one long tour, done
eras.text: With Doug Scharin on drums, Codeine made its most ambitious record in three studios, toured Europe, and stopped because the songs had.

years.cap: Stephen Immerwahr on bass at a club show
yt: Live at T.T. the Bear's, Cambridge, 1993
years.h: The White Birch arrives, and Spin gives it a 9 out of 10
years.p: Recorded in 1993 in Chicago, Middletown, Connecticut, and New York, with David Grubbs on guitar for Tom and Wird.
years.xp:
Clean guitars break into heavy distortion, a step away from the bare early sound. Select compared it to monks doing plainsong remixes.

The record is often cited as a template by bands like [[Low|42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24]] and [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]].

years.h: A long European tour, then Codeine just stops
years.p: Immerwahr says the band ended because the new songs stopped coming, plus some interpersonal stuff. He and John Engle took jobs at the Department of Health and in market research.
years.xp:
"The main reason why I think the band stopped is because it stopped going and there stopped being new songs," Immerwahr told the Village Voice.

He later left music for a career as a research scientist and formed Raymond. Doug Scharin went on to Rex, [[June of 44|56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f]] and HiM.

eras.title: Numero calls
eras.text: A reissue box brought the original trio back for a handful of shows. Playing that slow again turned out to be the hard part.

yt: Reunion set, Szene Wien, Vienna, November 18, 2012
years.h: Rehearsals go nowhere, then Codeine plays Alexandra Palace
years.p: The first reunion show is at I'll Be Your Mirror in London, with Stephen Immerwahr, John Engle and Chris Brokaw. The run ends July 15 at Le Poisson Rouge in New York.
years.xp: Engle says the first seven or eight rehearsals went nowhere. "Three people playing slowly is an entirely different matter," he told Brooklyn Vegan.

years.h: Numero Group collects everything in When I See the Sun
years.p: The box gathers Frigid Stars, Barely Real and The White Birch with rarities, including four songs from the shelved Dessau session.

eras.title: Thirty years late, and then goodbye
eras.text: The album Codeine threw away in 1992 finally came out. The band played what it said would be its last shows, then a few more abroad in 2024.

years.p: Numero Group releases the eight songs from Harold Dessau Recording. NPR's Sarah Hennies said it felt like a ghost in her living room.

years.cap: Codeine at Union Pool, Brooklyn, c. 2023
q: The shows we play this year will be our last.
yt: Live at The Echo, Los Angeles, December 8, 2023
years.h: Codeine plays Union Pool, its first show in 11 years
years.p: A week later they play the Numero Group's 20th anniversary festival in Los Angeles. Shows in Canada, Australia, Japan and Mexico follow in 2024.
years.xp:
Immerwahr said the 2023 shows would be the last because of his full-time job at the New York City Department of Health. "This isn't a return to being an active band. And I'm OK with that," he told Brooklyn Vegan.

He showed up in black metal T-shirts. Brokaw had recorded an acoustic version of a Vlad Tepes song.

years.h: Codeine dedicates Atmosphere to Low's Mimi Parker
years.p: The Joy Division cover goes to [[Mimi Parker|31e0783a-9c5d-4218-9f23-4b9427b111e7]], who died in November 2022. Codeine and [[Low|42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24]] had shared a Joy Division tribute album in the '90s.
years.xp: "There's always a sadness and loss when you play a Joy Division song, and Mimi's loss deepens it," Brokaw told Brooklyn Vegan.
